predecessors.name: Guiyi Circuit
predecessors.text: Ganzhou: 'Around the years 881 and 882, Ganzhou slipped from the control of the Guiyi Circuit'; in 874 the Wenmo, 'remnant forces of the Tibetan Empire', drove the Uyghurs out of Ganzhou

predecessors.name: Uyghur Khaganate
predecessors.text: 'There was a pre-existing community of Uyghurs at Ganzhou by 840 at the very latest'; refugees of the Uyghur Khaganate settled in Ganzhou, Suzhou and Shazhou

successors.name: Western Xia (Great Xia)
successors.text: 'In 1036 the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom was annexed by the Tanguts'

ledger.x: 894: Pangteqin founds the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom.
1036: the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom ends; its land passes to the Tanguts, whose Western Xia was proclaimed in 1038.

wars.name: Wenmo expulsion of the Ganzhou Uyghurs
wars.outcome: Remnant Tibetan forces known as the Wenmo drove the Uyghurs out of Ganzhou in 874; Ganzhou slipped from the Guiyi Circuit around 881-882 and the kingdom was established there in 894.

wars.name: Ganzhou attack on Jinshan
wars.outcome: The Ganzhou Uyghurs attacked the Kingdom of Jinshan (Guiyi) in 910 and 911 and forced it into an alliance as a lesser partner; no land is recorded.

wars.name: Guiyi-Ganzhou war of 925
wars.outcome: Cao Yijin attacked and defeated the Ganzhou Uyghurs after heavy fighting in 925; in 926 Aduoyu married Cao Yijin's daughter.

wars.name: Tangut and Liao wars against the Ganzhou Uyghurs
wars.outcome: The Tanguts attacked in 1003 and were beaten; the Uyghurs beat them again in 1008; the Liao attacked and defeated the Uyghurs in 1008 and 1010; the Uyghurs captured Liangzhou in 1009.

wars.name: Tangut conquest of the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom
wars.outcome: Defeated by the Liao in 1026 and by the Tanguts in 1028, Guazhou surrendered in 1030 and Shazhou in 1036; the kingdom was annexed in 1036.

certainty.note: A string of oasis cities along the Hexi and the Alxa steppe; no page gives a frontier, and Cliopatria's single shape is held for 140 years.
